course_position.stage_name: Toward B1 - Complex Conversations and Narratives

lesson_intent.one_sentence_goal: Practice the set phrase det sägs att for simple news or rumors.
lesson_intent.real_life_context: Colleagues mention a light news item or a workplace rumor without needing full certainty.
lesson_intent.communicative_function: Referring to something people say while keeping the source vague.

dialogue_task.scenario: Anna and Erik discuss a simple local news item or workplace update that people are talking about.

main_focus.name: set passive phrase det sägs att
main_focus.description: Use det sägs att to introduce information that is heard from others, without focusing on the speaker.
model_examples: Det sägs att kaféet ska öppna igen.
Det sägs att det blir kallare i helgen.
main_focus.desired_presence: Use det sägs att naturally 1-2 times, supported by simple discussion afterward.

allowed_supporting_grammar: future with ska or kommer att

vocabulary_target.theme: simple news and things people say
useful_chunks: Jag vet inte om det stämmer.
Vi får se vad som händer.
vocabulary_target.desired_presence: Use simple news chunks and keep the topic light and everyday.

dialogue_shape.opening: One speaker mentions having heard a small piece of news.
dialogue_shape.middle: They use det sägs att and discuss whether the information seems likely or useful.
dialogue_shape.ending: They leave the topic open or connect it to a practical plan.

target_complexity.repetition: one or two uses of the set phrase are enough

focus: the news or rumor being discussed
how certain or uncertain the information seems
what practical plan or expectation follows

sentence_focus: one sentence with det sägs att
one sentence with Har du hört att
one sentence expressing uncertainty about whether something is true
one sentence about a local place opening or closing
one sentence connecting a news item to a possible plan
